title: Household-level flood risk is concentrated among higher-income property owners, with uninsured low-income risk still important
discussion_signal: The NBER announcement corrects a simple flood-risk narrative: household-level exposure is disproportionately concentrated among higher-income property owners, while vulnerable uninsured low-income homeowners still face serious risk. The public signal makes aggregate floodplain disadvantage and household exposure separate questions.
linked_research_question: How do flood exposure, property ownership, insurance coverage, income, and mobility combine into unequal household risk, and where do aggregate floodplain measures mislead policy?
limits: The announcement is a short research translation rather than the full household analysis
Exposure, insurance, and realized loss are distinct outcomes
Public engagement cannot establish the prevalence or causal mechanism of the reported pattern
